3 weeks without Yofi
The saddest three weeks of my life.

I thought long and hard before writing this response, but I felt I had to. This is not a response born of anger, but one filled with indignation, powerlessness, and intense grief.
Three weeks ago, Yofi passed away here.
Yofi was a part of me, of my life, and of my history. He was 16 years and 8 months old. Yes, he was an old dog, but outwardly, he was still doing very well. He ate well, still walked, and even chased birds. Three weeks ago, before we went to the vet, we walked together in the park for half an hour. He was happy.
In the last month, one of Yofi's testicles had become enlarged. After examinations, everything pointed to a tumor, and neutering was recommended.

This vet was not our regular vet, but was recommended to us by a neighbor. Because the practice was close to home and we could get an appointment faster, we placed our trust in them. We knew that anesthesia carried risks.

Yofi had been under anesthesia three times before, the last time six months ago. Everything went well then.

Three weeks ago, Yofi was anesthetized again; he was neutered, woke up from the anesthesia, and a few minutes later he suffered a cardiac arrest.

At 12:45 p.m., the vet called me to say that I could pick up Yofi in about an hour. Everything had gone well. My little daughter and I were overjoyed.

At 1:45 p.m., I went to pick up Yofi.

Yofi had passed away.
"We don't know why..."

At that moment, my world collapsed.
For three weeks now, I have blamed myself for bringing him here.

To get answers, we should have taken him to Utrecht for an autopsy. But on that day, my life stood still. I lived as if I were in a movie, on autopilot, in complete denial. How is it possible that Yofi was running after birds one moment and was dead three hours later? I still can't believe it.

Yofi saved me so many times. And I couldn't protect him. It feels like I brought him to his death myself.
The pain is unbearable. I don't feel like doing anything anymore.
I knew this day would come someday, but I wasn't prepared for it. I took him to the vet so he could be helped.
He died without me, all alone, in a cold room, in a place he was terrified of.

I couldn't say goodbye to him.

I brought him here to be helped. What I got back was his lifeless body and a brochure from a crematorium.
I am sorry, Yofi. I am sorry, my dearest. I will never forgive myself for this.
